author: NorthEast News Desk
body: North Korea said Monday that a recent live-fire exercise involving missiles, artillery and drones demonstrated the country’s ability to combine several weapons systems, The Associated Press reported.

The exercise took place Saturday and was described by North Korean officials as a test of an integrated weapons-control system. South Korea’s military separately said it detected several short-range ballistic missiles launched from the eastern coastal area near Wonsan.

The missiles traveled about 250 kilometers, or roughly 155 miles, toward waters off North Korea, according to South Korean officials cited by AP. That range is consistent with systems designed to reach targets in South Korea, including U.S. military facilities.

North Korea’s claims about the exercise could not be independently verified. The drill came after a joint exercise involving the United States, South Korea and Japan, which Pyongyang has criticized as provocative.

The situation remains developing. Further statements from South Korean, U.S. or North Korean authorities could clarify the number of launches, the systems used and whether additional exercises are planned.
dek: North Korea said it conducted a live-fire exercise involving missiles, artillery and drones as South Korea reported short-range ballistic-missile launches.
headline: North Korea says live-fire drill demonstrated combined missile and drone power
